skill.name: video-edit
skill.description: Routes video-edit requests to the appropriate RunComfy model for restyling, background changes, packaging swaps, motion transfer, or outfit edits. Provides model-specific prompting guidance and CLI invocation patterns for RunComfy.
skill.summary: Choose and run the right RunComfy video edit model for the requested transformation.
skill.author: runcomfy-com

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally uses the RunComfy CLI for installation, authentication, model execution, remote polling, and output downloads. Most static findings are Markdown syntax, placeholder URLs, or documented safe credential storage rather than malicious behavior.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before installing packages, logging in, or running RunComfy model commands.
Warn users that prompts and media URLs are submitted to RunComfy services, and avoid sensitive content unless approved.
Keep token files owner-only and use secret-managed RUNCOMFY_TOKEN values in CI or containers.

content.user_title: Route Video Edits to RunComfy Models
content.value_statement: Video edit requests often need different models for restyle, motion control, or localized changes. This skill routes the task and supplies RunComfy prompts for the selected model.
actual_capabilities: Selects Wan 2.7 Edit-Video for general restyles, background swaps, packaging swaps, and commercial polish.
Selects Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control for motion transfer from reference clips.
Selects Lucy Edit Restyle for lightweight outfit swaps, lighting changes, and identity-stable restyles.
Provides required input fields, duration limits, resolution notes, and audio options for each route.
Shows RunComfy CLI invocation patterns with output directory handling.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, account authentication, and reachable media URLs.
Each edit uses one route; the skill does not blend multiple models in one call.
Model limits still apply, including duration, resolution, aspect ratio, and file size constraints.
Generated quality depends on source media, prompt specificity, and the selected RunComfy model.

use_cases.title: Restyle creator clips
use_cases.description: Turn a short talking-head clip into a branded scene while preserving face, pose, lip movement, and audio.

use_cases.title: Prepare product variants
use_cases.description: Swap packaging or background elements in a product video using a reference image and a focused edit direction.

use_cases.title: Transfer character motion
use_cases.description: Apply motion from a reference video to a target character for controlled animation tests.

prompt_templates.title: Restyle a short video
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner background swap with identity preservation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit this video with RunComfy: [video URL]. Preserve the subject face and motion. Change the background to [new setting]. Keep original audio.

prompt_templates.title: Swap product packaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the video-edit skill for this product clip: [video URL]. Use [reference image URL] for the new packaging. Preserve framing and hand movement.

prompt_templates.title: Transfer reference motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Route this as motion control. Apply the motion from [reference video URL] to [target character image or video URL]. Preserve identity and keep original sound if suitable.

prompt_templates.title: Compare routes before running
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this edit request and choose Wan, Kling, or Lucy before invoking RunComfy: [goal], [video URL], [optional reference asset]. Explain the route choice and expected limits.

output_examples.input: A creator asks to replace a talking-head background with a modern office while keeping speech intact.
output_examples.output: Selected Wan 2.7 Edit-Video because the request is a talking-head background swap. The prompt prioritizes preserving face, lip movement, and audio.

output_examples.input: A marketing team asks to change product packaging using a reference image.
output_examples.output: Selected Wan 2.7 Edit-Video with a reference image. The output plan preserves framing and hand movement while replacing only the packaging design.

output_examples.input: A designer asks to apply dance motion from one clip to a target character.
output_examples.output: Selected Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control because the main goal is motion transfer from a reference clip to a target character.

best_practices: State preservation goals before describing the visual change.
Use one edit direction per run to reduce drift.
Choose reference images only when the visual target must be copied.
anti_patterns: Combining outfit, background, camera, and lighting changes in one request.
Using motion control when the task is only a style or color change.
Sending sensitive or private media URLs to a third-party model service.

faq.question: Which models does this skill route to?
faq.answer: It routes to Wan 2.7 Edit-Video, Kling 2.6 Pro Motion Control, or Lucy Edit Restyle.

faq.question: Does it require a RunComfy account?
faq.answer: Yes. The RunComfy CLI must be installed and authenticated before model requests can run.

faq.question: Does my media leave my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. The RunComfy CLI submits requests and media URLs to RunComfy model services for processing.

faq.question: Can it edit long videos?
faq.answer: Only within each model limit. Wan supports short clips, Kling supports route-specific durations, and Lucy is capped at 720p.

faq.question: Can I force a specific model?
faq.answer: Yes. Name the model in the request. The skill also notes when a brand-specific skill may fit better.

faq.question: Should commands run automatically?
faq.answer: Review install, login, and RunComfy commands before execution. Also confirm that media URLs are approved for third-party processing.
